ORDER This misc.appeal, under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, has been filed against the award dated 22.02.2019 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gadarwara,
District Narsinghpur in MACC No.300024/2016.

entities.text:
Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gadarwara,
District Narsinghpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Since the factum of accident is not in dispute, therefore, it is suffice to mention here that deceased Ankit was travelling in an auto and because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Auto, it turned turtle and the deceased Ankit died on the spot.
The accident took place on 18.04.2016.
It is submitted by the counsel for the appellant that the claims Tribunal has wrongly taken the notional income of the deceased as Rs.5800/- per month.

The Auto was carrying 12 passengers i.e.
in excess of 3 passengers as the permit was issued for 3 + 1.
The Auto was not carrying fitness certificate.

However, it is fairly conceded that in an another M.A.No.2756/2020, which was filed by the appellant/Insurance Company in respect of another claim case arising out of the same accident,
the appeal filed by the Insurance Company with regard to the fitness, has already been rejected on the ground that the appellant has failed to prove that the offending Auto was not having valid fitness certificate at the time of accident.

Per contra, it is submitted by the respondents/claimants that although the Claims Tribunal has taken the notional income of the deceased as Rs.5,800/- per months but even as per the notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act, the monthly income of an unskilled labourer was Rs.6,950/-.
Thus, the Claim Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased on a lower side, but fairly conceded that no cross-objection or separate appeal has been filed for enhancement of compensation amount.
It is further submitted that in an another award arising out of the same accident, the appeal filed by the appellant has already been rejected.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

So far as the income of the deceased is concerned, the Claims Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased as Rs.5,800/-; whereas as per the notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act, the minimum monthly wages of an unskilled employee on the date of accident was Rs.6,950/-.
Therefore, it is clear that the Claims Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased on a lower side.
However, since no cross-objection or appeal has been filed for enhancement of compensation amount, therefore, the notional income fixed by the Claims Tribunal as Rs.5,800/- is hereby affirmed.

sentences.text: 2 So far as the ground raised by the appellant with regard to over-carrying of the passengers by the Tribunal is concerned, this Court is of the considered opinion that the case in hand is squarely covered by the order dated 18.11.2022 passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in M.A.No.2756/2020 by which the appellant was held liable to pay the compensation amount severally and jointly with the owner and driver of the vehicle.
So far as the fitness of Auto is concerned, the appellant has relied upon a certificate issued by the RTO (Ex.D.11 and D.12)
However, the appellant has not examined any officer from the RTO Office to prove the said document.
Admittedly, Indralal (D.W.3) examined by the Insurance Company was not an employee of the RTO Office, Narsinghpur, but he was an employee of the Insurance Company.

Since the certificate (Ex.D.11 and D.12) issued by the RTO Office were not proved by the Insurance Company,
therefore, the same cannot be relied upon.
Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that it is not possible for this Court to hold that the Auto was being driven without any fitness certificate.
It is next contended by the counsel for the appellant that the burden is on the Driver and Owner of the vehicle to prove the fitness certificate.

Once the appellant has decided to plead and prove that the Auto was not having the fitness certificate and also tried to get it proved by producing the certificate issued by the Insurance Company, then it cannot be said that in spite of having failed in proving that the Auto was not having fitness certificate, the burden to prove the same was on the Driver and Owner of the Auto.

Furthermore, the claim petition is between claimants and respondents and co- respondent, who has to indemnify the insured cannot say that the burden is not on it to prove that the vehicle was not having fitness certificate.
If the appellant claims that the offending vehicle was not having fitness certificate, then the burden is on appellant to prove the same.
No other argument is advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
Ex consequenti, the award dated 22.02.2019 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gadarwara, District Narsinghpur in MACC No.300024/2016 is hereby affirmed.
